title: Oven-Charred Braised Korean Pork Stew
description: A hearty, slow-cooked Korean stew from Gyeongsang province, featuring a sweet and savory Shio-koji-cured pork.

ingredients.name: Shio-koji-cured pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: available at Asian markets or online

instructions: Season the Shio-koji-cured pork shoulder with salt and black pepper.
In a large Dutch oven or clay pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Brown the pork shoulder on all sides, then remove it from the pot and set it aside.
Add the onion, ginger, and garlic to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened.
Add the Korean chili flakes, golden caster sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, and Korean chili paste to the pot.
Stir to combine and bring the sauce to a simmer.
Return the pork shoulder to the pot and cover it with a lid or aluminum foil.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven and braise the pork for 2 1/2 hours, or until tender.
Remove the pot from the oven and stir in the sesame oil.
Let the stew rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve the braised pork and sauce over a bed of steamed rice or noodles.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
